summary: A converter or quantizer that expects a `v_proj` weight on every global layer will not find one when `attention_k_eq_v` is true; mlx-lm creates `v_proj` only when `not use_k_eq_v`.

facts.text: A converter or quantizer that expects a `v_proj` weight on every global layer will not find one when `attention_k_eq_v` is true; mlx-lm creates `v_proj` only when `not use_k_eq_v`.
In mlx-lm's Gemma 4 text attention, `use_k_eq_v` is `attention_k_eq_v and not is_sliding`, and a source comment says it applies to the 26B and 31B models.
mlx-lm sets `values = keys` straight after `k_proj`, before `k_norm` and RoPE, and only creates a separate `v_proj` when `use_k_eq_v` is false.
mlx-lm applies `v_norm` (`RMSNormNoScale`) to values and `k_norm` plus RoPE to keys, so cached K and V differ under k_eq_v.
mlx-lm uses `num_global_key_value_heads` as the K/V head count on k_eq_v layers when that config field is not None.
mlx-lm sets the Gemma 4 attention scale to 1.0.

Hugging Face transformers names the flag `use_alternative_attention = config.attention_k_eq_v and not is_sliding`, sets `v_proj` to None in that case, and uses `value_states = key_states` before `k_norm`.
Hugging Face applies `v_norm = Gemma4RMSNorm(head_dim, with_scale=False)` to values, separate from the scaled `k_norm` on keys.

In transformers, KV-shared layers read `shared_kv_states[layer_type]` and have no `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `k_norm` or `v_norm`; the last non-shared layer of each attention type stores its full-length K/V into that dict.
Both implementations set the attention scaling to 1.0, so Gemma 4 relies on q_norm and k_norm instead of 1/sqrt(d) scaling.
